title: Backing Out a Settled Rider Claim Line and Recording What is Left Owing
content:
Where a claim line the rider has settled under one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is to be put right, it is backed out by posting a reversal of its own against that one line, rather than by altering the line itself.

## Invoking the reversal

The reversal is posted with `reverse_rider_benefit_line_9daedfb7`. The representative unlocks the tool and then calls it themselves.

### Parameters

- `source_claim_id` — Id class. The reference number of the single settled claim line being backed out, as it stands in the member's rider benefit claim history.
- `restated_member_share` — Fixed-format class. What the member is left owing on that line as it now stands, in USD to 2 decimal places, as a plain positive number with no currency sign. It is stored rounded to 2 decimal places, and an amount of zero is written as 0.00.

### What the posting does

The reversal carries over the line's date of service, benefit category, procedure, tooth, eye or ear reference, allowed amount and position in the submitted claim; it carries the negative of the benefit that line paid, stands as reversed, names the line it applies to, and is dated with today's date. What the member is left owing on the line as it now stands is recorded on the reversal. The benefit backed out is taken off the benefit the rider has paid toward this benefit year's maximum, so the member's remaining maximum rises by that much.

### Return

A confirmation sentence naming the reversal's own newly created reference number, the claim line it was posted against, the benefit backed out in USD as a negative number, what the member is left owing, and the benefit the rider has now paid toward this benefit year's maximum. The sentence being returned at all is what indicates the reversal has been posted.

## Basis Q&A

**Is the settled line itself altered?** No. A reversal of its own is posted against that one line.

**What does the reversal carry as the benefit?** The negative of the benefit the line it applies to had paid.

**What happens to the member's remaining benefit year maximum?** The benefit backed out is taken off what the rider has paid toward this benefit year's maximum, so the remaining maximum rises by that much.
